# jobtriage CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_skill_refs.py. Do not edit: run the generator. -->

Every command, argument and flag, read from the parser itself. Run
`jobtriage COMMAND --help` for the same text in a terminal.

Global options come before the command:

    jobtriage --workspace PATH list --json

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--workspace` `PATH` | — | use this op folder (default: the nearest one — see `jobtriage init`) |
| `--version` | — | print the version, the workspace path and the database schema version |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | — | log at DEBUG on stderr; every command also writes &lt;op&gt;/.jobtriage/logs/jobtriage.log |

## `jobtriage scrape`

scrape the boards and run the pipeline (default: all)

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-s`, `--source` `BOARD` | `all` | job board to scrape (by name or alias), or "all" to query every board in parallel (default: all); the boards are the built-ins plus &lt;op&gt;/scrapers/ |
| `[limit]` | — | how many jobs to scrape per board (default: search.limit in jobtriage.toml, 50) |
| `--all` | — | include jobs restricted to specific countries (default: the configured locations) |
| `--raw` | — | list every scraped job unfiltered and save nothing (the pre-filter behaviour) |
| `--explain` | — | per board, report fetched, dropped by age/title (with the top reasons) and kept |

## `jobtriage sources`

the job boards: list, inspect, scaffold, test and enable/disable

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | — | print the listing as one JSON document: boards plus the broken map |

**Subcommands**

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `jobtriage sources info` | one board: docstring, terms, location vocabulary and recent_jobs options |
| `jobtriage sources new` | write &lt;op&gt;/scrapers/NAME.py from the shipped _example.py template |
| `jobtriage sources test` | run a board (or every enabled board) with limit 5 and report contract problems |
| `jobtriage sources enable` | remove a board from [sources].disabled (aliases are canonicalised) |
| `jobtriage sources disable` | add a board to [sources].disabled (aliases are canonicalised) |

## `jobtriage list`

list the newest jobs in the database, don't scrape

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[limit]` | `50` | how many jobs to show (default: 50) |
| `--status` `SLUG` | — | only jobs with this status (new, skipped, to_apply, applied) |
| `--since` `WINDOW` | — | only jobs published in the last N days, like 7d (undated jobs count by first seen) |
| `--source` `SOURCE` | — | only jobs from this board |
| `--search` `TEXT` | — | only jobs whose title, company, role or URL contains TEXT |
| `--order` `COL` | `published` | sort by one of company, first_seen, id, last_seen, published, salary, source, status, title (default: published) |
| `--limit` `N` | — | how many jobs to show (the flag form of the positional limit) — dest `limit_flag` |
| `--json` | — | print the jobs as JSON, one list of full job dicts (for agents and scripts) |

## `jobtriage show`

show one job in full: every field, notes, history

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ID` | — | the job id, as `jobtriage list --json` prints it |
| `--json` | — | print the job, its history and attachments as one JSON object |

## `jobtriage open`

open a job's posting in the workspace browser (the TUI's opener)

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ID` | — | the job id, as `jobtriage list --json` prints it |

## `jobtriage status`

set a job's status: new, skipped, to_apply, applied

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ID` | — | the job id, as `jobtriage list --json` prints it |
| `STATUS` | — | the status slug to set: new, skipped, to_apply, applied |

## `jobtriage note`

append a note to one job (keep a diary of it)

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ID` | — | the job id, as `jobtriage list --json` prints it |
| `TEXT` | — | the note; quote it if it has spaces |

## `jobtriage attach`

record a file (a cover letter, a PDF) against a job

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ID` | — | the job id, as `jobtriage list --json` prints it |
| `PATH` | — | the file; a relative path resolves from the op folder (letters/... works) |
| `--kind` `KIND` | — | what it is (default: cover_letter under letters/, else file) |

## `jobtriage export`

write the jobs as CSV or JSON, for a spreadsheet

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--format` `FORMAT` | `csv` | output format (default: csv) — one of `csv`, `json` |
| `--status` `SLUG` | — | only jobs with this status (new, skipped, to_apply, applied) |
| `--since` `WINDOW` | — | only jobs published in the last N days, like 7d (undated jobs count by first seen) |
| `--source` `SOURCE` | — | only jobs from this board |
| `--search` `TEXT` | — | only jobs whose title, company, role or URL contains TEXT |
| `--order` `COL` | `published` | sort by one of company, first_seen, id, last_seen, published, salary, source, status, title (default: published) |
| `--limit` `N` | — | at most N jobs (default: all of them) |

## `jobtriage config`

the op folder config: show, edit, get, set, validate

**Subcommands**

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `jobtriage config show` | print the effective config and the layer each value came from |
| `jobtriage config edit` | open jobtriage.toml in $EDITOR (or vi) and validate it afterwards |
| `jobtriage config get` | print one effective value: the loaded config, not just the file |
| `jobtriage config set` | set one file value, keeping comments (TOML value, else a bare string) |
| `jobtriage config validate` | load the config and print ok, or the first error |

## `jobtriage filter`

inspect the title filter: test a title against the config

**Subcommands**

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `jobtriage filter test` | say why the config would keep or drop a title (exit 0 kept, 1 dropped) |

## `jobtriage db`

the database: path, sqlite3 shell, schema, sheet import

**Subcommands**

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `jobtriage db path` | print the database file path |
| `jobtriage db shell` | run sqlite3 on the database; extra args go to sqlite3 |
| `jobtriage db schema` | print the tables and columns with comments |
| `jobtriage db import-sheet` | import the old Google Sheet CSV (one-time, then delete) |

## `jobtriage skills`

the agent skills: list them and install them for an agent

**Subcommands**

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `jobtriage skills list` | show the shipped, workspace and globally installed skills |
| `jobtriage skills install` | copy the workspace skills into an agent user-level folder (--global) |

## `jobtriage mcp`

run the MCP server over stdio, for agents without skill support

## `jobtriage tui`

the triage TUI: open, re-status, mark applied

## `jobtriage init`

create or upgrade the workspace (the op folder)

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[path]` | — | the folder to use (default: ~/jobtriage) |
| `--yes` | — | take the defaults, ask nothing (for scripts and agents) |
| `--upgrade` | — | refresh shipped assets in an existing workspace: replace the untouched, keep the edited (new version beside them as &lt;file&gt;.new) |

## `jobtriage doctor`

check the workspace, config, database, browser, plugins, skills, profile and boards; say how to fix what is wrong

| Argument / flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--offline` | — | skip the checks that depend on this machine and the network: the browser, its CDP port and the per-board homepage request (local checks only) |

## `jobtriage where`

print the workspace path (handy for scripts and agents)

## Exit codes and errors

- `0` — success (and, for `filter test`, "the title is kept").
- `1` — a runtime failure: a missing job, a broken config or board, a
  database that cannot be read or is from a newer build. `filter test`
  also uses 1 for "the title is dropped".
- `2` — usage: argparse's own errors (a missing argument, an unknown
  command, a bad number), an unknown status slug, an unknown board name.

Every failure is one line beginning `error:` on stderr; stdout stays
clean so a `--json` document can be piped. A command whose table has a
`--json` flag (or `export --format json`) is the machine-readable
surface; the write commands print a short confirmation instead.
